symptom: On Mendix 9.x a workflow with a user task made the project unloadable. exec reported 'Created workflow', then mx check 9.24.30 and Studio Pro died with `TypeCacheUnknownTypeException: The type cache does not contain a type with qualified name Workflows$SingleUserTaskActivity`. The same happened on 10.11.0 (measured), and on all of 10.0–10.11 by the SDK's version data
cause: userTaskToGen (and the ALTER mutator's inserts, through it) writes Workflows$SingleUserTaskActivity / MultiUserTaskActivity, TYPES introduced in 10.12.0, which also deleted Workflows$UserTask (mendixmodelsdk 4.117.0). The generated version data holds property floors only, so nothing compared the written $Type with the project's version. Before 10.12 the kind of task is the UserTask's UserTaskCompletion (9.22): SingleInputCompletion, or MultiInputCompletion {CompletionCriteria, TargetUserInput, AwaitAllUsers from 10.2}
file: `modelsdk/canon/versionshape_usertask.go` (lowerUserTaskType, dropTaskBoundaryEvents, userTaskActivitySince, completionCriteriaSince), `mdl/backend/modelsdk/workflow_read.go` (UserTask case reads the MultiInputCompletion), `mdl/executor/validate_workflow_rewrite.go` (rawMultiUserTaskSettings sees a 9.x multi-user task)
insight: **A type rename can also be a restructure.** Converting MultiUserTaskActivity down is more than a $Type swap. Three of its keys move into a nested MultiInputCompletion, and the outcomes stay on the task, so the CompletionCriteria's outcome pointers still resolve. Studio Pro 9.24.3's key set is the target: Multilevel Dynamic Workflow (Marketplace 221741) stores `$ID,$Type,Annotation,AutoAssignSingleTargetUser,Caption,DueDate,Name,OnCreatedEvent,Outcomes,TaskDescription,TaskName,TaskPage,UserSource,UserTaskCompletion`. **With no Studio Pro sample of a 9.x multi-user task, convert UP as the oracle.** The 9.24 output, after `mx convert -p` 10.24.24, has user tasks identical in keys and values to what mxcli writes on 10.24 directly, rule and participants included. **Every reader of the old shape needs the restructure too.** describe read a 9.x multi-user task as a single one, and the create-or-modify guard looked for the rule only on MultiUserTaskActivity, so a 9.24 rewrite would reset the rule silently. **Give an element the lowering ADDS a derived $ID** (completionID from the task's $ID), so the same task lowers to the same bytes. The boundary events on a user task (10.14, declared on the abstract UserTaskActivity) slipped past the floor the same way: an empty list is dropped below 10.14, and a boundary event is refused. Measured: bug-test on fresh apps. 9.24.30 before TypeCacheUnknownTypeException, after 0 errors. `mx convert -p` 9.24.30 changes no key and no value. describe → exec 'Unchanged workflow'. 10.24.24 and 11.13.0 give 0 errors. The CE2513 'Java 11' after converting up is in an untouched 9.24 app too. 10.11.0.37074 (downloaded for this, then deleted): before (lowering stubbed) TypeCacheUnknownTypeException, which confirms the SDK's 10.12 type boundary on the platform. After, 0 errors with AwaitAllUsers in the MultiInputCompletion, mx convert 10.11 changes nothing, and describe → exec 'Unchanged workflow'. Majority, await all users and a microflow rule written on 10.11 check clean. Control: stubbing lowerUserTaskType fails TestNormalize_UserTaskIsAWorkflowsUserTaskBelowMendix10_12, …MultiUserTask… and …RefusesWhatAnOlderUserTaskCannotHold with the 10.12 types on 9.24. The reader and guard tests failed before their fixes. Tests: those three, TestNormalize_UserTaskCompletionIDIsStable, TestWorkflowRead_UserTaskInTheMendix9Shape, TestWorkflowRewrite_SeesAMendix9MultiUserTasksSettings; mdl-examples/bug-tests/1771-user-task-below-10-12.mdl
